$comment: THE CAGE THAT TRAVELS. Everything here is the same on every machine, so this file is in version control and never moves once it is written. WHAT IS NOT HERE IS THE GUARD'S HTTP DOOR, and that is the whole reason there are two files. The door is a port, the port is per folder, and a per-machine number in a tracked file is dirt on every clone and a wrong number on all but one of them: this box committed 33987 and a cloud clone bound 30268, so the branch carried one box's port and every other box rewrote it before doing anything. The door lives in .claude/settings.local.json, which is not in version control. Claude Code merges list keys across settings files rather than picking one, so the two files are one cage, and it reloads hooks when a settings file changes, so a door written after the session began still arrives. SessionStart and the wake stay commands, because they are what brings the engine up, and neither needs a port to say so. WHAT EACH EVENT FIRES IS COUNTED IN src/cage/hooks-the-harness-fires.md, which carries the spike's table with the marks it was missing. Twelve of the fourteen events were seen to arrive under the editor and nine of those under the command line. Every other cell is unmeasured rather than silent: three command line cells nothing could have been recorded in, both compact events, the desktop Code tab, which was never driven, and copilot, which is registered no hooks. So no event registered here is one a harness was proven never to send, because that table proves nothing silent. util/checks/the-cage-cites-what-is-here.mjs holds this comment to sources a reader can open. Why an event is registered only where the guard owns the decision is [[a-hook-is-taken-only-when-level-0-owns-the-decision]].
$remoteControl: REMOTE CONTROL IS OFF UNLESS SOMEBODY TURNS IT ON. The key below is remoteControlAtStartup, and it belongs here rather than in .claude/settings.json because this file is projected over that one: a setting typed into the target is gone the next time the engine projects, which is what happened twice. Claude Code honours a false in project settings and IGNORES a true there, so a checked-in false is a one-way off switch: it cannot turn remote control ON for anybody who opens this repo, and it outranks a managed true. Turning it on stays a per-person choice, made in the app rather than in a file that travels. Why it is here at all: the toggle in the desktop app writes to the user's own settings and Claude Code saves the choice back there, so a person who turns it off finds it on again. See https://code.claude.com/docs/en/settings-reference#remotecontrolatstartup
$env: FUNCTION HOOKS ARE BEHIND A ROLLOUT FLAG, AND THIS IS THE DOCUMENTED WAY PAST IT. Claude Code asks GrowthBook whether tengu_plugin_hooks_modules is on and defaults it to false, so a box that is not in the wave loads no hooks module and does not register the plugin-types command. The client reads CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_FUNCTION_HOOKS first and that answer wins, so setting it here turns the feature on for every box that clones this tree, the cloud included, rather than for whoever remembered to export it. IT BELONGS IN THE TRAVELLING CAGE AND NOT IN THE PROJECTED FILE, because this file is written over that one and a key typed into the target is gone at the next start. THE CHECK IS PRESENCE AND NOT VALUE: the client tests whether the variable is defined, so a 0 here would also turn it on and only deleting the key turns it off. A client older than 2.1.259 reads no such variable and stays on whatever the flag says.
